text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The recent meeting between German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin in Berlin has produced a number of pragmatic answers to the rhetorical question "what to do with Russia".
- Turkmenistan has officially expressed disagreement with the oil agreement signed by Russia and Azerbaijan last week. Russian officials refrain from comments.
- The Federation Council, the upper chamber of parliament, has approved a package of economic laws which are likely to be signed by the President.
- Russia's UNEXIM Bank is prepared to fight with foreign rivals if necessary for the former state stake in the Norilsk Nikel factory which is to be auctioned soon.
- LUKoil is likely to acquire the 85 percent state-owned stake of one of Russia's biggest oil refineries, AO NORSI.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov's cherished idea of auctioning the government's foreign cars has been sabotaged by bureaucrats. But Nemtsov is determined to go on with it.
- The "shuttle diplomacy" of Russian national security official Boris Berezovsky may bring positive results in settling the conflict between Georgia and its breakaway region of Abkhazia.
- Russia is prepared to limit its steel exports to the United States if U.S. officials drop anti-dumping procedures against Russian metal producers.
- With Russian President Boris Yeltsin absent from NATO's summit in Madrid, the Western defence alliance can openly state that the second wave of expansion is unavoidable.

- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who has received "a power of attorney" from the Kremlin to rule the country for two months while the president is on vacation, has begun shifting the emphasis of domestic policy slightly.
- No previous NATO summit has been convened in such an unclear atmosphere of serious diagreement between the alliance members, says the paper in a comment on today's NATO summit in Madrid.
